name: Kodagu
headline: Even a girl who passed SSLC was engaged at 16 and later killed, showing marriage pressure after Class 10.
summary: Kodagu coverage includes a 16-year-old, the only student from her remote village school to pass SSLC, who was engaged immediately and later murdered. Child marriage cases stood at 10 in January-October 2025. The report's remark about elephant attacks on estate workers does not concern students and was not used.

reasons.detail: A 16-year-old who was the only student from her village school to pass SSLC was forced into an engagement and later murdered.
Estates in Kodagu depend on labourers, many migrating from North India, throughout the year; the report documents their hardship, though it does not itself quantify children's school exits.
A POCSO case alleged an estate owner sexually assaulted a minor girl living in an estate line house and facilitated her marriage; officials who failed to act were also booked.
A 2024 case involved a Class X girl whose families had agreed to defer marriage after Child Helpline intervention, showing early-marriage pressure on schoolgirls.
A Zilla Panchayat CEO visited Kadagadalu in Madikeri to collect dropout details and readmit a child to Class 8 in a government high school during a special enrolment drive.

responses.text: Zilla Panchayat CEO personally collected dropout information in Kadagadalu gram panchayat and persuaded parents to send children back as part of an education department enrolment drive.
Revaluation and supplementary exams helped Kodagu students: 25 failed candidates passed and 68 passed students sat improvement exams across two centres per taluk in 2025.
